title: Does a market that became large within the last 24 months have a manufacturable-dataset opportunity that the pre-existing literature does not already occupy?

scope.one_line: One round. Candidates enumerated and checked first-hand in session, no subagents. A market-timing screen, not a white-space screen.
scope.corpus: Public literature, dataset and repository indices reachable from this container.
scope.seed: Rounds 1-4 banked under preregistrations 0001 and 0002, plus the two large-market probes recorded in this session.
scope.rungs: Not applicable - this preregistration governs a SEARCH verdict, not a curve.
scope.what_this_does_not_cover: It does not cover ACCESS-based opportunities, because the founder has no proprietary corpus. It does not measure anything - a qualifying candidate here has passed a SCREEN, not an experiment, and would still need its own preregistration and its own measured A1/A2/F5 before any claim. It cannot overturn preregistrations 0001 or 0002. And it carries no claim of breadth: one session enumerating markets is not a market survey.

candidate_qualifies.passes_if: count of candidates with a dated citable market event within 24 months AND no open dataset at >=10^6 labelled units AND fewer than 2 serious efforts postdating that event AND prior_efforts recorded AND manufacturable labels with the mechanism named AND a stated asymmetry AND bytes_per_unit*1e6 <= 20e9  >=  1

market_event_age.passes_if: the dated market event is <= 24 months before 2026-08-25

post_event_efforts.passes_if: fewer than 2 serious efforts dated AFTER the market event target the same task at scale

arms: THE RIVAL EXPLANATION, run as an arm: for every candidate, search explicitly for work DATED AFTER the market event. If the field has already caught up, the timing thesis is false for that candidate and it dies - that is the arm that could refute this entire round.
PRE-EVENT LITERATURE, recorded but not disqualifying. A candidate whose pre-event literature is enormous is still suspect, and the count is banked so a reader can disagree with the ruling.
THE DATE ITSELF: a market event must be a regulation taking effect, a standard being finalised, or a product category appearing - with a URL. 'The market is growing' is refused.
stop_rules: If no candidate qualifies, that is written down as NO_MARKET_TIMED_CANDIDATE_FOUND and this line of search is closed. No fifth reformulation of the criterion under this preregistration.
A qualifying candidate has passed a SCREEN and nothing more. It gets its own preregistration and its own measured A1, A2 and F5 before any claim is made about it.
If a candidate's market event cannot be dated to a citable source, it fails, however large the market obviously is.

why_this_search_differs.finding_that_prompted_it: Across 99 candidates in rounds 1-3, plus two large-market probes run afterwards (synthetic-speech source tracing, video-encoder settings recovery), the pattern is mechanistic: LARGE BUYER IMPLIES CROWDED. Markets attract researchers. The carved-DEFLATE candidate has a hole because forensic fragment attribution is a SMALL market. Speech source tracing has MLAAD, DiffSSD and STOPA plus an Interspeech special session; video parameter recovery has 98.88%-accuracy CRF prediction and an H.264 fragment-parameter paper. Both closed.
why_this_search_differs.the_three_escapes: A large buyer and an open hole coexist in exactly three situations: TIMING (the market became large recently and the field has not caught up), ACCESS (the data is locked up and you have it), or CAPABILITY (it just became technically possible). FDM-1 was timing plus capability - computer-use agents became a large market at the same moment the method became feasible. The founder has no ACCESS advantage, so only timing and capability are available.
why_this_search_differs.what_changes: Rounds 1-4 hunted UNSTUDIED problems. This round hunts RECENTLY-FUNDED ones, and treats pre-existing literature as non-disqualifying when it predates the money.
why_this_search_differs.the_risk_being_bounded: That is a genuine LOOSENING of G4 after four negative results, which is exactly how a bar slips. The loosening is therefore bounded here, before any candidate is examined: only work DATED AFTER the market event counts against a candidate, the event must be specific, dated and citable with a URL, and pre-event work must still be searched for and RECORDED even though it does not disqualify.
